title: Determinants for the use of IL-1-Inhibitors in the treatment of Familial Mediterranean Fever
summary: Familial Mediterranean Fever (FMF) is the most common genetic disorder caused by dysregulation of the immune system. Patients experience recurrent febrile episodes. Colchicine is the standard therapy. However, some patients develop a colchicine resistance. In such cases, IL-1-blocking therapy is required. The central research question is which factors are associated with colchicine resistance and indicate the need for IL-1 inhibitor treatment. Disease activity will be assessed using the PRAS and ISSF scores. In addition, a descriptive analysis of genetic data, clinical and laboratory parameters, comorbidities, and disease course will be conducted.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients in whom Familial Mediterranean Fever was diagnosed and treated with IL-1-blocking therapy between 2004 and 2025.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Diagnosis of Familial Mediterranean Fever according to the Tel Hashomer criteria
3, Treatment in the Department of Rheumatology at the University Hospital Heidelberg (UKHD) between 01.01.2004, and 31.12.2025
3. Treatment with IL-1-inhibitors
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients who have not yet reached the age of 18
2. Incomplete patient records that preclude the analysis of indicators for IL-1 inhibitor therapy
3. Patients treated outside the UKHD or without documented treatment in the Department of Rheumatology
4. Patients without a documented follow-up visit
